source_documents.source_document: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Fever in Children

exact_sections.heading: 1. Background
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines pediatric fever assessment context and the importance of age, measurement site, appearance, persistence, and underlying disease.

exact_sections.heading: 2. Scope; 3. Purpose; 4. Applicability
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines Dubai telehealth pediatric fever scope and emergency exclusions.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 Virtual Clinical Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Prioritises airway, breathing, circulation, consciousness, age-specific risk, and illness-severity assessment.

exact_sections.heading: 7. Referral Criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Uses risk features to guide emergency referral, specialist assessment, or explicitly documented safety-netting.

source_documents.population: Children with fever.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed health facilities.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Bedwetting in under 19s

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.20 — assessment and investigation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting onset, prior dryness, bedwetting pattern, daytime urinary symptoms, toileting and fluid intake, comorbidities, clinically selected urinalysis or referral context, and findings from history without autonomous diagnosis.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.3 and 1.4.1–1.4.2 — information and management planning
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording information given, family priorities, support needs and clinician-entered management or follow-up discussion without selecting treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.10–1.3.15 and 1.8–1.9 — referral, response and recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting severe daytime symptoms, recurrent infection, suspected physical or neurological problems, referral or review and recurrence context without automated escalation.

source_documents.population: Children and young people under 19 with bedwetting.
source_documents.setting: Primary, community and specialist assessment and management of bedwetting.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Food allergy in under 19s: assessment and diagnosis

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.4 — assessment and allergy-focused clinical history
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting symptom systems, age and speed of onset, duration, severity, frequency, setting, reproducibility, suspected food, exposure amount, atopic and feeding history, prior treatment and growth or examination findings.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.5–1.1.11 — IgE-mediated and non-IgE-mediated diagnosis
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-selected skin-prick or specific-IgE testing, test limitations, elimination and reintroduction discussion and result review without interpreting results or generating treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.12 and referral recommendations — information, support and specialist care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting information about suspected allergy, severe-reaction risk, diagnostic process, support and clinician-entered referral or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Children and young people under 19 with suspected food allergy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, community and specialist food-allergy assessment.

population: Infants, children and adolescents requiring clinician-led acute assessment or follow-up.
setting: Paediatric primary care and urgent assessment.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Fever in Children

exact_sections.heading: 1. Background
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines pediatric fever assessment context and the importance of age, measurement site, appearance, persistence, and underlying disease.

exact_sections.heading: 2. Scope; 3. Purpose; 4. Applicability
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines Dubai telehealth pediatric fever scope and emergency exclusions.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 Virtual Clinical Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Prioritises airway, breathing, circulation, consciousness, age-specific risk, and illness-severity assessment.

exact_sections.heading: 7. Referral Criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Uses risk features to guide emergency referral, specialist assessment, or explicitly documented safety-netting.

source_documents.population: Children with fever.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed health facilities.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Bedwetting in under 19s

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.20 — assessment and investigation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting onset, prior dryness, bedwetting pattern, daytime urinary symptoms, toileting and fluid intake, comorbidities, clinically selected urinalysis or referral context, and findings from history without autonomous diagnosis.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.3 and 1.4.1–1.4.2 — information and management planning
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording information given, family priorities, support needs and clinician-entered management or follow-up discussion without selecting treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.10–1.3.15 and 1.8–1.9 — referral, response and recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting severe daytime symptoms, recurrent infection, suspected physical or neurological problems, referral or review and recurrence context without automated escalation.

source_documents.population: Children and young people under 19 with bedwetting.
source_documents.setting: Primary, community and specialist assessment and management of bedwetting.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Food allergy in under 19s: assessment and diagnosis

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.4 — assessment and allergy-focused clinical history
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting symptom systems, age and speed of onset, duration, severity, frequency, setting, reproducibility, suspected food, exposure amount, atopic and feeding history, prior treatment and growth or examination findings.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.5–1.1.11 — IgE-mediated and non-IgE-mediated diagnosis
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-selected skin-prick or specific-IgE testing, test limitations, elimination and reintroduction discussion and result review without interpreting results or generating treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.12 and referral recommendations — information, support and specialist care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting information about suspected allergy, severe-reaction risk, diagnostic process, support and clinician-entered referral or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Children and young people under 19 with suspected food allergy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, community and specialist food-allergy assessment.

population: Infants, children and adolescents requiring clinician-led acute assessment or follow-up.
setting: Paediatric primary care and urgent assessment.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.15–1.5.17 — monitoring and referral after acute kidney injury
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording serum-creatinine monitoring after AKI, stability or degree of renal function at discharge, and clinician-considered nephrology referral context.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.4 — information, support and future care after AKI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting monitoring, prognosis, self-management, renal-replacement information, dehydration and medicine-risk discussion without generating advice automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Quality statement 6 — clinical review after hospital discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting that discharge plans identify AKI and the timing and responsibility for follow-up clinical review.

source_documents.population: Adults, children and young people with or recovering from acute kidney injury.
source_documents.setting: Hospital discharge planning, outpatient renal follow-up and primary or specialist monitoring.

source_documents.source_organisation: UK Kidney Association
source_documents.source_document: Vascular Access for Haemodialysis

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access assessment and monitoring
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, relevant vascular-access assessment and monitoring recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

population: Adults requiring kidney-function, electrolyte, dialysis or renal follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.3.7 — seizure assessment, EEG, and imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-event and witness history, physical examination, ECG or metabolic context, EEG review, MRI review, recurrence after remission, and specialist assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1.1–2.1.11 — information, safety, and daily impact
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports trigger, adherence, side-effect, safety, driving, employment or education, reproductive-health, and care-plan discussions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.1.1–4.5.11 — treatment, monitoring, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-control and adverse-effect review, clinician-led medication and interaction review, antiseizure medication levels when indicated, care review, and pregnancy-related specialist review without mapping a dose.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 7.1.1–7.3.1 — status, cluster, and prolonged seizure plans
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documentation of seizure clusters or convulsive emergencies and a clinician-agreed individual emergency management plan without mapping emergency medication or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 10.1.1–10.2.2 — epilepsy-related death and SUDEP risk
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure frequency, adherence, alcohol or drug use, uncontrolled seizures, abnormal neurological findings, and clinician-documented risk and safety discussion.

source_documents.population: Children, young people, and adults with suspected or established epilepsy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, specialist, emergency, and ongoing epilepsy care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.7 — secondary prevention after confirmed TIA
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led secondary-prevention planning after specialist confirmation of TIA without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.4 — brain and carotid imaging after specialist TIA assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed MRI and carotid imaging in the specified specialist-assessment context.

source_documents.population: People aged over 16 years with suspected or confirmed stroke or transient ischaemic attack.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, specialist TIA assessment, imaging, and secondary-prevention planning.

population: Adults with neurological symptoms, results or follow-up needs.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.3.7 — seizure assessment, EEG, and imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-event and witness history, physical examination, ECG or metabolic context, EEG review, MRI review, recurrence after remission, and specialist assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1.1–2.1.11 — information, safety, and daily impact
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports trigger, adherence, side-effect, safety, driving, employment or education, reproductive-health, and care-plan discussions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.1.1–4.5.11 — treatment, monitoring, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-control and adverse-effect review, clinician-led medication and interaction review, antiseizure medication levels when indicated, care review, and pregnancy-related specialist review without mapping a dose.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 7.1.1–7.3.1 — status, cluster, and prolonged seizure plans
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documentation of seizure clusters or convulsive emergencies and a clinician-agreed individual emergency management plan without mapping emergency medication or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 10.1.1–10.2.2 — epilepsy-related death and SUDEP risk
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure frequency, adherence, alcohol or drug use, uncontrolled seizures, abnormal neurological findings, and clinician-documented risk and safety discussion.

source_documents.population: Children, young people, and adults with suspected or established epilepsy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, specialist, emergency, and ongoing epilepsy care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.7 — secondary prevention after confirmed TIA
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led secondary-prevention planning after specialist confirmation of TIA without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.4 — brain and carotid imaging after specialist TIA assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed MRI and carotid imaging in the specified specialist-assessment context.

source_documents.population: People aged over 16 years with suspected or confirmed stroke or transient ischaemic attack.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, specialist TIA assessment, imaging, and secondary-prevention planning.

population: Adults with neurological symptoms, results or follow-up needs.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.3.7 — seizure assessment, EEG, and imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-event and witness history, physical examination, ECG or metabolic context, EEG review, MRI review, recurrence after remission, and specialist assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1.1–2.1.11 — information, safety, and daily impact
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports trigger, adherence, side-effect, safety, driving, employment or education, reproductive-health, and care-plan discussions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.1.1–4.5.11 — treatment, monitoring, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-control and adverse-effect review, clinician-led medication and interaction review, antiseizure medication levels when indicated, care review, and pregnancy-related specialist review without mapping a dose.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 7.1.1–7.3.1 — status, cluster, and prolonged seizure plans

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 10.1.1–10.2.2 — epilepsy-related death and SUDEP risk
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure frequency, adherence, alcohol or drug use, uncontrolled seizures, abnormal neurological findings, and clinician-documented risk and safety discussion.

source_documents.source_document: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.3.7 — seizure assessment, EEG, and imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-event and witness history, physical examination, ECG or metabolic context, EEG review, MRI review, recurrence after remission, and specialist assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1.1–2.1.11 — information, safety, and daily impact
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports trigger, adherence, side-effect, safety, driving, employment or education, reproductive-health, and care-plan discussions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.1.1–4.5.11 — treatment, monitoring, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-control and adverse-effect review, clinician-led medication and interaction review, antiseizure medication levels when indicated, care review, and pregnancy-related specialist review without mapping a dose.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 7.1.1–7.3.1 — status, cluster, and prolonged seizure plans
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documentation of seizure clusters or convulsive emergencies and a clinician-agreed individual emergency management plan without mapping emergency medication or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 10.1.1–10.2.2 — epilepsy-related death and SUDEP risk
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure frequency, adherence, alcohol or drug use, uncontrolled seizures, abnormal neurological findings, and clinician-documented risk and safety discussion.

source_documents.population: Children, young people, and adults with suspected or established epilepsy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, specialist, emergency, and ongoing epilepsy care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.7 — secondary prevention after confirmed TIA
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led secondary-prevention planning after specialist confirmation of TIA without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.4 — brain and carotid imaging after specialist TIA assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed MRI and carotid imaging in the specified specialist-assessment context.

source_documents.population: People aged over 16 years with suspected or confirmed stroke or transient ischaemic attack.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, specialist TIA assessment, imaging, and secondary-prevention planning.

population: Adults with neurological symptoms, results or follow-up needs.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.3.7 — seizure assessment, EEG, and imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-event and witness history, physical examination, ECG or metabolic context, EEG review, MRI review, recurrence after remission, and specialist assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1.1–2.1.11 — information, safety, and daily impact
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports trigger, adherence, side-effect, safety, driving, employment or education, reproductive-health, and care-plan discussions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.1.1–4.5.11 — treatment, monitoring, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure-control and adverse-effect review, clinician-led medication and interaction review, antiseizure medication levels when indicated, care review, and pregnancy-related specialist review without mapping a dose.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 7.1.1–7.3.1 — status, cluster, and prolonged seizure plans
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documentation of seizure clusters or convulsive emergencies and a clinician-agreed individual emergency management plan without mapping emergency medication or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 10.1.1–10.2.2 — epilepsy-related death and SUDEP risk
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports seizure frequency, adherence, alcohol or drug use, uncontrolled seizures, abnormal neurological findings, and clinician-documented risk and safety discussion.

source_documents.population: Children, young people, and adults with suspected or established epilepsy.
source_documents.setting: Primary, specialist, emergency, and ongoing epilepsy care.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.7 — secondary prevention after confirmed TIA
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led secondary-prevention planning after specialist confirmation of TIA without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.4 — brain and carotid imaging after specialist TIA assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed MRI and carotid imaging in the specified specialist-assessment context.

source_documents.population: People aged over 16 years with suspected or confirmed stroke or transient ischaemic attack.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, specialist TIA assessment, imaging, and secondary-prevention planning.

population: Adults with neurological symptoms, results or follow-up needs.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Annex 4 — visual loss and other urgent presentations

exact_sections.heading: Screening test, grading and result communication
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording bilateral visual acuity, image status, grading, screening outcome and result letters sent to the person and relevant clinicians.

exact_sections.heading: Surveillance and hospital-eye-service pathway
exact_sections.locator: section 2 Screening test; surveillance and referral requirements
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-confirmed surveillance, ungradable-image, digital-surveillance or hospital-eye-service referral status without autonomously assigning a grade or destination.

exact_sections.heading: Sections 1.2 and 5.1 — common eyelid symptoms and styes

exact_sections.heading: Section 5.3 — blepharitis

exact_sections.heading: Section 9 — referral criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral, worsening, vision change, severe redness, severe pain, photophobia, spread, trauma, uncertain diagnosis, and refractory-symptom documentation without automatically concluding urgency.

source_documents.population: People with eyelid swelling, including stye, chalazion, blepharitis, allergy, infection, trauma, and lesion differentials, with telehealth exclusions.

population: Adults and children requiring eye-symptom or vision follow-up documentation.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Menopause: identification and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Menopause: identification and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically
