source_documents.source_document: Menopause: identification and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Menopause: identification and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Menopause: identification and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.6 — information and support
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists menstrual-cycle changes, vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, musculoskeletal, and sexual symptoms and their variable severity and duration.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.6 — identifying perimenopause and menopause
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines symptom-and-cycle-based identification in people aged 45 or over and limits laboratory and imaging tests, including FSH in specified contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — discussing management options
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires benefit-risk discussion tailored to age, circumstances, risk factors, preferences, and repeated review when HRT is chosen.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.5–1.5.13 — genitourinary symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-discussed moisturiser, lubricant, and vaginal-treatment options and ongoing review for genitourinary symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.9.1–1.9.3 — reviewing treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines documented review at three months, annually thereafter, or earlier for ineffectiveness, adverse effects, or clinical need.

source_documents.population: Women, trans men, and non-binary people registered female at birth with menopause-associated symptoms.
source_documents.setting: Primary and specialist care.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
source_documents.source_document: The Initial Management of Chronic Pelvic Pain — Green-top Guideline No. 41

exact_sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope; 2. Background; 5. Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic pelvic pain as a symptom rather than a diagnosis and frames initial assessment around the woman’s concerns, function, and multifactorial context.

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 History; 5.2 Examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies pain pattern, menstrual, bladder, bowel, movement, posture, function and medication history plus abdominal and pelvic examination for focal tenderness or structural findings.

exact_sections.heading: 6.1 Screening for Infection; 6.2 Transvaginal Scanning and MRI
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-selected STI sampling when PID is suspected and transvaginal ultrasound for adnexal masses and selected chronic pelvic-pain pathology.

source_documents.population: Women presenting for the first time with chronic pelvic pain of at least 6 months that is not pregnancy-related.
source_documents.setting: General gynaecology and primary-care referral assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: World Health Organization
source_documents.source_document: Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, fourth edition

exact_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose; 1.2 Scope; 1.3 Target audience
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines the guideline as practical contraceptive-use guidance for providers once medical eligibility has been established.

exact_sections.heading: 1.5 Contraceptive choice and informed consent
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires understandable information, voluntary informed choice, client preference, consent, and freedom from coercion.

exact_sections.heading: 1.6 Quality of care and access to products
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies method information on effectiveness, correct use, common effects, risks and benefits, return-to-clinic signs, fertility, STI protection, and opportunities for questions.

exact_sections.heading: 3.1 Examinations and tests; 3.2 Contraceptive eligibility; 5.1 Reasonable certainty that a woman is not pregnant
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines method-specific examination and test classification, preserves medical eligibility as a separate assessment, and supports pregnancy-status review before method initiation.

exact_sections.heading: Method-specific continuation, common effects and return guidance
exact_sections.locator: fourth edition method chapters and recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the method actually used, adherence or continuation, entered bleeding or other effects, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review. It does not diagnose an adverse reaction or select a replacement method.

exact_sections.heading: Emergency contraceptive pills and copper-bearing intrauterine devices for emergency contraception
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting intercourse timing, method discussion, pregnancy possibility and clinician-selected emergency-contraception care with method and eligibility qualifiers retained; it does not autonomously select or provide a method.

exact_sections.heading: Contraceptive implants — initiation, continuation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified implant, insertion date or site, bleeding or other entered concerns, satisfaction and clinician-arranged review with pregnancy and eligibility qualifiers retained.

exact_sections.heading: Copper-bearing and levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine devices — initiation and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an identified device, insertion details, strings or examination actually assessed, bleeding or pain, pregnancy and infection context, and clinician-arranged follow-up without asserting correct position or selecting removal.

source_documents.population: People seeking initiation, continuation, switching, or support for contraceptive method use after medical eligibility is established.
source_documents.setting: Contraceptive counselling and service delivery.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led reproductive or pelvic-health review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

source_documents.source_document: Urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse in women: management

exact_sections.heading: Assessing urinary incontinence — history and physical examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urgency-incontinence or overactive-bladder symptom context, relevant contributing factors, and clinician-performed pelvic-floor assessment in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Urine testing, residual urine, and bladder diaries
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urine dipstick, qualified culture, post-void residual, and bladder-diary documentation in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Indications for referral to a specialist service
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified bladder, urethral, voiding, neurological, haematuria, or recurrent unexplained UTI contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Lifestyle and behavioural interventions
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting caffeine or fluid discussion and bladder training only when discussed or arranged by the clinician for qualified adult women.

source_documents.population: Women aged 18 and over with urinary incontinence or overactive-bladder symptoms, with UTI, voiding, referral, and treatment qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, urine testing, bladder diaries, conservative management, and specialist referral.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management

exact_sections.heading: Diagnostic imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed CT or ultrasound imaging with age and pregnancy qualifiers.

exact_sections.heading: Metabolic testing
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports stone analysis, serum-calcium context, and qualified paediatric specialist metabolic assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Preventing recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting hydration or dietary context and prevention advice only when discussed by the clinician; numeric instructions are not mapped.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people with suspected or confirmed renal or ureteric stones, with age and pregnancy qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Assessment, imaging, procedural management, metabolic testing, prevention, and follow-up of renal and ureteric stones.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

population: Adults requiring urinary-symptom, stone or urological follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

source_documents.source_document: Urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse in women: management

exact_sections.heading: Assessing urinary incontinence — history and physical examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urgency-incontinence or overactive-bladder symptom context, relevant contributing factors, and clinician-performed pelvic-floor assessment in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Urine testing, residual urine, and bladder diaries
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urine dipstick, qualified culture, post-void residual, and bladder-diary documentation in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Indications for referral to a specialist service
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified bladder, urethral, voiding, neurological, haematuria, or recurrent unexplained UTI contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Lifestyle and behavioural interventions
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting caffeine or fluid discussion and bladder training only when discussed or arranged by the clinician for qualified adult women.

source_documents.population: Women aged 18 and over with urinary incontinence or overactive-bladder symptoms, with UTI, voiding, referral, and treatment qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, urine testing, bladder diaries, conservative management, and specialist referral.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management

exact_sections.heading: Diagnostic imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed CT or ultrasound imaging with age and pregnancy qualifiers.

exact_sections.heading: Metabolic testing
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports stone analysis, serum-calcium context, and qualified paediatric specialist metabolic assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Preventing recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting hydration or dietary context and prevention advice only when discussed by the clinician; numeric instructions are not mapped.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people with suspected or confirmed renal or ureteric stones, with age and pregnancy qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Assessment, imaging, procedural management, metabolic testing, prevention, and follow-up of renal and ureteric stones.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

population: Adults requiring urinary-symptom, stone or urological follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Assessing urinary incontinence — history and physical examination
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urgency-incontinence or overactive-bladder symptom context, relevant contributing factors, and clinician-performed pelvic-floor assessment in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Urine testing, residual urine, and bladder diaries
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports urine dipstick, qualified culture, post-void residual, and bladder-diary documentation in adult women.

exact_sections.heading: Indications for referral to a specialist service
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified bladder, urethral, voiding, neurological, haematuria, or recurrent unexplained UTI contexts.

exact_sections.heading: Lifestyle and behavioural interventions
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting caffeine or fluid discussion and bladder training only when discussed or arranged by the clinician for qualified adult women.

source_documents.population: Women aged 18 and over with urinary incontinence or overactive-bladder symptoms, with UTI, voiding, referral, and treatment qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment, urine testing, bladder diaries, conservative management, and specialist referral.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management

exact_sections.heading: Diagnostic imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed CT or ultrasound imaging with age and pregnancy qualifiers.

exact_sections.heading: Metabolic testing
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports stone analysis, serum-calcium context, and qualified paediatric specialist metabolic assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Preventing recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting hydration or dietary context and prevention advice only when discussed by the clinician; numeric instructions are not mapped.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people with suspected or confirmed renal or ureteric stones, with age and pregnancy qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: Assessment, imaging, procedural management, metabolic testing, prevention, and follow-up of renal and ureteric stones.

source_documents.source_document: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — dizziness and vertigo in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports focal neurological and hearing red flags, acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS by trained clinicians, neuroimaging referral, and Hallpike assessment for positional vertigo.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.10 and 1.10.1–1.10.6 — limb weakness and sensory symptoms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden, progressive, fluctuating, unilateral, symmetrical, sensory-associated, and back-pain-associated weakness, urgent referral, and clinician-led imaging where specified.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.10.1–1.10.13 — sensory symptoms including tingling or numbness in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports sudden unilateral numbness, rapidly progressive symmetrical sensory change with weakness or imbalance, recurrent sensory episodes, distal sensory distribution, reflex and gait context, selected metabolic tests, radicular symptoms, bowel or bladder context, and clinician-led referral.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.15.1–1.15.4 — tremor in adults
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports rest or asymmetric tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait difficulty, symmetrical postural tremor, medicine, thyroid and alcohol review, functional impact, head tremor, and clinician-led referral.

source_documents.population: Adults aged over 16 years with suspected neurological conditions.
source_documents.setting: Initial assessment and referral from primary or community care.

population: Adults requiring urinary-symptom, stone or urological follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 Virtual Clinical Assessment; Common Features
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers itch, dry skin, erythema, vesicles, crusting, scaling, excoriation, lichenification, fissuring, age-linked distribution, atopy, sleep, and quality-of-life impact.

exact_sections.heading: 7. Red Flags
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists non-blanching rash, rapidly worsening painful eczema, fever or lethargy, respiratory distress, clustered blisters, punched-out erosions, recurrent infection, pregnancy, and psychosocial concerns.

exact_sections.heading: 8. Diagnosis
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports morphology and distribution review, atopy history, dry skin, selected non-routine tests, and differential-diagnosis assessment.

exact_sections.heading: 10. Management
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-led trigger reduction, skin-barrier care, education, and pharmacological choices; no medicine dose is mapped.

source_documents.population: Children and adults with atopic dermatitis complaints.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed health facilities.

source_documents.source_document: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Allergic Contact Dermatitis

exact_sections.heading: Sections 1, 5, 6 and 9 — risks, morphology, distribution, symptoms, diagnosis, and history
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports contact-dermatitis terminology, itch, burning, erythema, scale, vesicles, blistering, edema, weeping, distribution, exposure, occupation, products, temporal course, atopy, and clinician-observed morphology.

exact_sections.heading: Sections 7 and 13 — red flags and referral criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports fever or systemic illness, respiratory distress, rapidly worsening painful eczema, recurrent or spreading infection, extensive involvement, pregnancy, and clinician-led return or referral documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Section 9 — patch testing, laboratory tests, photographs, and histopathology
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed exposure history, photographs, patch testing, KOH or culture, and selected tests when diagnosis is uncertain, without recommending testing automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Sections 11–12 — clinician-led avoidance, skin care, and treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting trigger avoidance, skin-care or emollient discussion, and clinician-stated topical treatment without mapping medicine names, doses, frequency, duration, or autonomous advice.

source_documents.population: People with suspected or clinician-diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis, including occupational, home, hobby, topical-product, and age-related exposure contexts.
source_documents.setting: DHA-licensed telehealth assessment with face-to-face, family-physician, or dermatology referral where indicated.

exact_sections.heading: Atopic eczema triggers

exact_sections.heading: 5.1 Virtual Clinical Assessment; Common Features
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers itch, dry skin, erythema, vesicles, crusting, scaling, excoriation, lichenification, fissuring, age-linked distribution, atopy, sleep, and quality-of-life impact.

exact_sections.heading: 7. Red Flags
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists non-blanching rash, rapidly worsening painful eczema, fever or lethargy, respiratory distress, clustered blisters, punched-out erosions, recurrent infection, pregnancy, and psychosocial concerns.

exact_sections.heading: 8. Diagnosis
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports morphology and distribution review, atopy history, dry skin, selected non-routine tests, and differential-diagnosis assessment.

exact_sections.heading: 10. Management
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-led trigger reduction, skin-barrier care, education, and pharmacological choices; no medicine dose is mapped.

source_documents.population: Children and adults with atopic dermatitis complaints.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed health facilities.

source_documents.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
source_documents.source_document: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Allergic Contact Dermatitis

exact_sections.heading: Sections 1, 5, 6 and 9 — risks, morphology, distribution, symptoms, diagnosis, and history
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports contact-dermatitis terminology, itch, burning, erythema, scale, vesicles, blistering, edema, weeping, distribution, exposure, occupation, products, temporal course, atopy, and clinician-observed morphology.

exact_sections.heading: Sections 7 and 13 — red flags and referral criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports fever or systemic illness, respiratory distress, rapidly worsening painful eczema, recurrent or spreading infection, extensive involvement, pregnancy, and clinician-led return or referral documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Section 9 — patch testing, laboratory tests, photographs, and histopathology
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed exposure history, photographs, patch testing, KOH or culture, and selected tests when diagnosis is uncertain, without recommending testing automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Sections 11–12 — clinician-led avoidance, skin care, and treatment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting trigger avoidance, skin-care or emollient discussion, and clinician-stated topical treatment without mapping medicine names, doses, frequency, duration, or autonomous advice.

source_documents.population: People with suspected or clinician-diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis, including occupational, home, hobby, topical-product, and age-related exposure contexts.
source_documents.setting: DHA-licensed telehealth assessment with face-to-face, family-physician, or dermatology referral where indicated.

source_documents.source_document: Atopic eczema

exact_sections.heading: Symptoms of atopic eczema
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording itch, dry or cracked skin, rash distribution and flare symptoms as patient-reported context.

exact_sections.heading: Atopic eczema triggers
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting reported irritants, trigger context and flare pattern without inferring causation.

exact_sections.heading: When to get medical help
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting advice-seeking and clinician review prompts for worsening or infected eczema symptoms.

source_documents.population: People with atopic eczema, including children and adults.
source_documents.setting: Public-facing condition information for symptom recognition, self-care and when to seek clinical advice.

population: Adults and children requiring clinician-led skin assessment or follow-up.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Standards 3-5 - frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and cognition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty status for older or at-risk surgical patients, comprehensive geriatric assessment when performed, and cognition assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations for primary care, surgical outpatients, and preoperative assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty score, nutrition and BMI, comorbidities, cognition, medicines, functional status, reassessment, and individualized shared decisions.

source_documents.population: Adults living with or at risk of frailty who are undergoing elective or emergency surgery.
source_documents.setting: Referral, surgical outpatient, preoperative assessment, ward, theatre, recovery, discharge, and community transfer.

source_documents.source_document: Medicines optimisation: the safe and effective use of medicines to enable the best possible outcomes — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Medicines-related communication between care settings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports complete and accurate medicine information, prescribed and non-prescribed medicines, allergies, timing, monitoring, and discussion at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines reconciliation as identifying an accurate current medicine list, comparing records, recognising discrepancies, documenting changes, and including over-the-counter or complementary medicines.

exact_sections.heading: Medication review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports structured review of all medicines, views, understanding, concerns, questions, adherence context, adverse-reaction or side-effect context, monitoring, and circumstances for seeking professional advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.2–1.3.7 — transfer information and medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.5 — involvement, values, preferences, benefits, and harms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the person’s desired involvement, values, preferences, and clinician-completed discussion of treatment options, benefits and harms without generating a medicine decision.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people using medicines, with specific transfer, reconciliation, and decision-involvement recommendations.
source_documents.setting: Transfers between care settings and clinician-led medicines consultations.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

population: Older adults requiring function, frailty or medication review.

exact_sections.heading: Standards 3-5 - frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and cognition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty status for older or at-risk surgical patients, comprehensive geriatric assessment when performed, and cognition assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations for primary care, surgical outpatients, and preoperative assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty score, nutrition and BMI, comorbidities, cognition, medicines, functional status, reassessment, and individualized shared decisions.

source_documents.population: Adults living with or at risk of frailty who are undergoing elective or emergency surgery.
source_documents.setting: Referral, surgical outpatient, preoperative assessment, ward, theatre, recovery, discharge, and community transfer.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Medicines optimisation: the safe and effective use of medicines to enable the best possible outcomes — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Medicines-related communication between care settings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports complete and accurate medicine information, prescribed and non-prescribed medicines, allergies, timing, monitoring, and discussion at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines reconciliation as identifying an accurate current medicine list, comparing records, recognising discrepancies, documenting changes, and including over-the-counter or complementary medicines.

exact_sections.heading: Medication review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports structured review of all medicines, views, understanding, concerns, questions, adherence context, adverse-reaction or side-effect context, monitoring, and circumstances for seeking professional advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.2–1.3.7 — transfer information and medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.5 — involvement, values, preferences, benefits, and harms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the person’s desired involvement, values, preferences, and clinician-completed discussion of treatment options, benefits and harms without generating a medicine decision.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people using medicines, with specific transfer, reconciliation, and decision-involvement recommendations.
source_documents.setting: Transfers between care settings and clinician-led medicines consultations.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

population: Older adults requiring function, frailty or medication review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty status for older or at-risk surgical patients, comprehensive geriatric assessment when performed, and cognition assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations for primary care, surgical outpatients, and preoperative assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty score, nutrition and BMI, comorbidities, cognition, medicines, functional status, reassessment, and individualized shared decisions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines-related communication between care settings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports complete and accurate medicine information, prescribed and non-prescribed medicines, allergies, timing, monitoring, and discussion at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines reconciliation as identifying an accurate current medicine list, comparing records, recognising discrepancies, documenting changes, and including over-the-counter or complementary medicines.

exact_sections.heading: Medication review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports structured review of all medicines, views, understanding, concerns, questions, adherence context, adverse-reaction or side-effect context, monitoring, and circumstances for seeking professional advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.2–1.3.7 — transfer information and medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.5 — involvement, values, preferences, benefits, and harms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the person’s desired involvement, values, preferences, and clinician-completed discussion of treatment options, benefits and harms without generating a medicine decision.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people using medicines, with specific transfer, reconciliation, and decision-involvement recommendations.
source_documents.setting: Transfers between care settings and clinician-led medicines consultations.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

population: Older adults requiring function, frailty or medication review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Standards 3-5 - frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and cognition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty status for older or at-risk surgical patients, comprehensive geriatric assessment when performed, and cognition assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations for primary care, surgical outpatients, and preoperative assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty score, nutrition and BMI, comorbidities, cognition, medicines, functional status, reassessment, and individualized shared decisions.

source_documents.population: Adults living with or at risk of frailty who are undergoing elective or emergency surgery.
source_documents.setting: Referral, surgical outpatient, preoperative assessment, ward, theatre, recovery, discharge, and community transfer.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Medicines optimisation: the safe and effective use of medicines to enable the best possible outcomes — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Medicines-related communication between care settings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports complete and accurate medicine information, prescribed and non-prescribed medicines, allergies, timing, monitoring, and discussion at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines reconciliation as identifying an accurate current medicine list, comparing records, recognising discrepancies, documenting changes, and including over-the-counter or complementary medicines.

exact_sections.heading: Medication review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports structured review of all medicines, views, understanding, concerns, questions, adherence context, adverse-reaction or side-effect context, monitoring, and circumstances for seeking professional advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.2–1.3.7 — transfer information and medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.5 — involvement, values, preferences, benefits, and harms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the person’s desired involvement, values, preferences, and clinician-completed discussion of treatment options, benefits and harms without generating a medicine decision.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people using medicines, with specific transfer, reconciliation, and decision-involvement recommendations.
source_documents.setting: Transfers between care settings and clinician-led medicines consultations.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

population: Older adults requiring function, frailty or medication review.

exact_sections.heading: Standards 3-5 - frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and cognition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty status for older or at-risk surgical patients, comprehensive geriatric assessment when performed, and cognition assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations for primary care, surgical outpatients, and preoperative assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting frailty score, nutrition and BMI, comorbidities, cognition, medicines, functional status, reassessment, and individualized shared decisions.

source_documents.population: Adults living with or at risk of frailty who are undergoing elective or emergency surgery.
source_documents.setting: Referral, surgical outpatient, preoperative assessment, ward, theatre, recovery, discharge, and community transfer.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Medicines optimisation: the safe and effective use of medicines to enable the best possible outcomes — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Medicines-related communication between care settings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports complete and accurate medicine information, prescribed and non-prescribed medicines, allergies, timing, monitoring, and discussion at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines reconciliation as identifying an accurate current medicine list, comparing records, recognising discrepancies, documenting changes, and including over-the-counter or complementary medicines.

exact_sections.heading: Medication review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports structured review of all medicines, views, understanding, concerns, questions, adherence context, adverse-reaction or side-effect context, monitoring, and circumstances for seeking professional advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.2–1.3.7 — transfer information and medicines reconciliation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.5 — involvement, values, preferences, benefits, and harms
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the person’s desired involvement, values, preferences, and clinician-completed discussion of treatment options, benefits and harms without generating a medicine decision.

source_documents.population: Adults, children, and young people using medicines, with specific transfer, reconciliation, and decision-involvement recommendations.
source_documents.setting: Transfers between care settings and clinician-led medicines consultations.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

population: Older adults requiring function, frailty or medication review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: SAMPLE history and emergency disposition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports signs and symptoms, allergies, medicines, past history, last intake, events or mechanism, examination, interventions, reassessment, and disposition documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Trauma secondary survey
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports inspection for wounds, bruising, swelling, tenderness, deformity, range of movement, neurological findings, severe pain, and other injury signs.

exact_sections.heading: Extremity trauma and perfusion
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports deformity, distal pulse, capillary refill, sensation, neurovascular compromise, open fracture, splinting, and perfusion reassessment documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Open wound and laceration assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports laceration or abrasion, location, size and depth, bleeding, contamination, foreign-body concern, underlying structures, distal perfusion, dressing, splinting, tetanus, and return or disposition documentation.

source_documents.population: Adults and children with acute illness or injury presenting to first-contact emergency care.
source_documents.setting: First-contact emergency units and resource-limited emergency-care settings.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Emergency Medicine
source_documents.source_document: Management of Investigation Results in the Emergency Department

exact_sections.heading: Summary and pathology/radiology recommendations — traceable review and responsibility
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports a traceable record of review, action, responsibility, referral and handover for pathology and radiology results.

exact_sections.heading: Operational guidance — result review, patient communication, record and follow-up action
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the specific test, reviewed result or report, communication and clinician-determined follow-up action.

source_documents.population: Adults and children whose pathology or radiology investigations were requested or reviewed by an emergency department.
source_documents.setting: Emergency department result review, communication, handover and follow-up governance.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led critical-care review or transition documentation.

exact_sections.heading: SAMPLE history and emergency disposition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports signs and symptoms, allergies, medicines, past history, last intake, events or mechanism, examination, interventions, reassessment, and disposition documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Trauma secondary survey
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports inspection for wounds, bruising, swelling, tenderness, deformity, range of movement, neurological findings, severe pain, and other injury signs.

exact_sections.heading: Extremity trauma and perfusion
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports deformity, distal pulse, capillary refill, sensation, neurovascular compromise, open fracture, splinting, and perfusion reassessment documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Open wound and laceration assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports laceration or abrasion, location, size and depth, bleeding, contamination, foreign-body concern, underlying structures, distal perfusion, dressing, splinting, tetanus, and return or disposition documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Mental-health audit standards for the emergency department
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting triage, current self-harm or suicide risk, leaving risk, capacity for a decision to leave, prior psychiatric history, mental-state examination and referral or follow-up when performed.

exact_sections.heading: Mental Health Triage and Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current presenting state, agitation, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness to accept care, observation level and care-plan status; it explicitly warns triage is not a future-risk prediction tool.

source_documents.population: Adults and children presenting to emergency departments with mental illness, self-harm risk or mental-health crisis.
source_documents.setting: Emergency mental-health triage, initial assessment, documentation, observation and liaison working.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Depression in adults: treatment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — recognition, comprehensive assessment, function, and context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting low mood, loss of interest, duration, course, functional, interpersonal and social difficulty, previous mood history, physical and mental comorbidity, sleep, stressful events, medicines, substances, loneliness and support.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.8–1.2.12 — clinician-completed risk assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording that suicidal ideation, intent, support and immediate risk were directly assessed by a competent clinician; it does not populate a negative, assign risk, or generate escalation.

source_documents.population: Adults with possible or diagnosed depression; communication and carer involvement are qualified.
source_documents.setting: Primary and mental healthcare recognition and assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1–1.5.17 — psychosocial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording the person’s needs, concerns, strengths, vulnerabilities, context and clinician-performed psychosocial assessment without using a prediction score.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.12–1.7.20 — emergency-department initial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting injury severity, emotional and mental state, distress, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness for care, observation and care-plan status in the ED.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.2 and 1.9.6 — safeguarding and discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording safeguarding consideration and clinician-confirmed assessment, plan, communication and follow-up before discharge after self-harm.

source_documents.population: Children, young people and adults who have self-harmed, unless a recommendation is age-specific.
source_documents.setting: Community, emergency department, hospital and mental-health care following self-harm.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led mental-health assessment or follow-up.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Mental-health audit standards for the emergency department
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting triage, current self-harm or suicide risk, leaving risk, capacity for a decision to leave, prior psychiatric history, mental-state examination and referral or follow-up when performed.

exact_sections.heading: Mental Health Triage and Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current presenting state, agitation, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness to accept care, observation level and care-plan status; it explicitly warns triage is not a future-risk prediction tool.

source_documents.population: Adults and children presenting to emergency departments with mental illness, self-harm risk or mental-health crisis.
source_documents.setting: Emergency mental-health triage, initial assessment, documentation, observation and liaison working.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Depression in adults: treatment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — recognition, comprehensive assessment, function, and context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting low mood, loss of interest, duration, course, functional, interpersonal and social difficulty, previous mood history, physical and mental comorbidity, sleep, stressful events, medicines, substances, loneliness and support.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.8–1.2.12 — clinician-completed risk assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording that suicidal ideation, intent, support and immediate risk were directly assessed by a competent clinician; it does not populate a negative, assign risk, or generate escalation.

source_documents.population: Adults with possible or diagnosed depression; communication and carer involvement are qualified.
source_documents.setting: Primary and mental healthcare recognition and assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1–1.5.17 — psychosocial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording the person’s needs, concerns, strengths, vulnerabilities, context and clinician-performed psychosocial assessment without using a prediction score.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.12–1.7.20 — emergency-department initial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting injury severity, emotional and mental state, distress, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness for care, observation and care-plan status in the ED.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.2 and 1.9.6 — safeguarding and discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording safeguarding consideration and clinician-confirmed assessment, plan, communication and follow-up before discharge after self-harm.

source_documents.population: Children, young people and adults who have self-harmed, unless a recommendation is age-specific.
source_documents.setting: Community, emergency department, hospital and mental-health care following self-harm.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led mental-health assessment or follow-up.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically
