exact_sections.heading: Mental Health Triage and Initial Assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current presenting state, agitation, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness to accept care, observation level and care-plan status; it explicitly warns triage is not a future-risk prediction tool.

source_documents.population: Adults and children presenting to emergency departments with mental illness, self-harm risk or mental-health crisis.
source_documents.setting: Emergency mental-health triage, initial assessment, documentation, observation and liaison working.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Depression in adults: treatment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — recognition, comprehensive assessment, function, and context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting low mood, loss of interest, duration, course, functional, interpersonal and social difficulty, previous mood history, physical and mental comorbidity, sleep, stressful events, medicines, substances, loneliness and support.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.8–1.2.12 — clinician-completed risk assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording that suicidal ideation, intent, support and immediate risk were directly assessed by a competent clinician; it does not populate a negative, assign risk, or generate escalation.

source_documents.population: Adults with possible or diagnosed depression; communication and carer involvement are qualified.
source_documents.setting: Primary and mental healthcare recognition and assessment.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1–1.5.17 — psychosocial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording the person’s needs, concerns, strengths, vulnerabilities, context and clinician-performed psychosocial assessment without using a prediction score.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.12–1.7.20 — emergency-department initial assessment and care
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting injury severity, emotional and mental state, distress, immediate safety, safeguarding, willingness for care, observation and care-plan status in the ED.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.2 and 1.9.6 — safeguarding and discharge
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording safeguarding consideration and clinician-confirmed assessment, plan, communication and follow-up before discharge after self-harm.

source_documents.population: Children, young people and adults who have self-harmed, unless a recommendation is age-specific.
source_documents.setting: Community, emergency department, hospital and mental-health care following self-harm.

population: Adults requiring clinician-led mental-health assessment or follow-up.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: 6. Red Flags and 7. Clinical Manifestation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports usage-related joint pain, stiffness, motion restriction, tenderness, swelling, instability, functional limitation, night pain, fever, redness or heat, weight loss, and systemic concern features.

exact_sections.heading: 8.1.4 Knee and 8.1.5 Hip
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Describes knee pain location, stairs-related pain, giving way, instability, and hip groin or thigh pain, stiffness, walking pain, restricted movement, and early loss of internal rotation.

exact_sections.heading: 9. Diagnosis and Imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines clinical diagnosis in typical adults, cautions that radiographic findings may not match symptoms, and limits MRI or other imaging to selected uncertainty or alternative-diagnosis contexts.

exact_sections.heading: 11. Referral Criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines concern and specialist contexts including a hot swollen joint, persistent fever, night symptoms, weight loss, face-to-face assessment needs, worsening symptoms, severe functional limitation, and selected imaging.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

exact_sections.heading: 6. Red Flags and 7. Clinical Manifestation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports usage-related joint pain, stiffness, motion restriction, tenderness, swelling, instability, functional limitation, night pain, fever, redness or heat, weight loss, and systemic concern features.

exact_sections.heading: 8.1.4 Knee and 8.1.5 Hip
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Describes knee pain location, stairs-related pain, giving way, instability, and hip groin or thigh pain, stiffness, walking pain, restricted movement, and early loss of internal rotation.

exact_sections.heading: 9. Diagnosis and Imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines clinical diagnosis in typical adults, cautions that radiographic findings may not match symptoms, and limits MRI or other imaging to selected uncertainty or alternative-diagnosis contexts.

exact_sections.heading: 11. Referral Criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines concern and specialist contexts including a hot swollen joint, persistent fever, night symptoms, weight loss, face-to-face assessment needs, worsening symptoms, severe functional limitation, and selected imaging.

source_documents.population: Adults with osteoarthritis symptoms, particularly middle-aged and older adults.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed healthcare facilities.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Neuropathic pain in adults: pharmacological management in non-specialist settings

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.7 — assessment, treatment planning, referral, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports pain severity, daily activity, sleep, participation, physical and psychological wellbeing, medicine response and adverse effects, coping, clinician-led treatment planning, early and regular review, and specialist referral without mapping medicine names or doses.

source_documents.population: Adults with neuropathic pain managed in non-specialist settings.
source_documents.setting: Non-specialist assessment, treatment review, and specialist referral.

population: Adults requiring inflammatory, musculoskeletal or disease-modifying treatment review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: 6. Red Flags and 7. Clinical Manifestation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports usage-related joint pain, stiffness, motion restriction, tenderness, swelling, instability, functional limitation, night pain, fever, redness or heat, weight loss, and systemic concern features.

exact_sections.heading: 8.1.4 Knee and 8.1.5 Hip
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Describes knee pain location, stairs-related pain, giving way, instability, and hip groin or thigh pain, stiffness, walking pain, restricted movement, and early loss of internal rotation.

exact_sections.heading: 9. Diagnosis and Imaging
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines clinical diagnosis in typical adults, cautions that radiographic findings may not match symptoms, and limits MRI or other imaging to selected uncertainty or alternative-diagnosis contexts.

exact_sections.heading: 11. Referral Criteria
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines concern and specialist contexts including a hot swollen joint, persistent fever, night symptoms, weight loss, face-to-face assessment needs, worsening symptoms, severe functional limitation, and selected imaging.

source_documents.population: Adults with osteoarthritis symptoms, particularly middle-aged and older adults.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed healthcare facilities.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Multimorbidity: clinical assessment and management — Recommendations

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

source_documents.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
source_documents.source_document: Neuropathic pain in adults: pharmacological management in non-specialist settings

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.7 — assessment, treatment planning, referral, and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports pain severity, daily activity, sleep, participation, physical and psychological wellbeing, medicine response and adverse effects, coping, clinician-led treatment planning, early and regular review, and specialist referral without mapping medicine names or doses.

source_documents.population: Adults with neuropathic pain managed in non-specialist settings.
source_documents.setting: Non-specialist assessment, treatment review, and specialist referral.

population: Adults requiring inflammatory, musculoskeletal or disease-modifying treatment review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

source_documents.source_organisation: Royal College of Emergency Medicine and Royal College of General Practitioners

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the clinician-confirmed diagnosis or outcome and plan, patient understanding, specifically required follow-up and safety-net communication.

exact_sections.heading: GP Communication and example discharge-letter headings
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording the presenting complaint, investigations or procedures, outcome, follow-up, responsible party, referral and discharge destination in a discharge handover.

source_documents.population: Adult and pediatric patients being discharged directly from an emergency department.
source_documents.setting: Emergency-department discharge communication with patients and primary care.

exact_sections.heading: 1. Background
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Identifies severity-risk contexts and distinguishes uncomplicated common cold from other respiratory presentations.

exact_sections.heading: 2. Scope; 3. Purpose; 4. Applicability
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines Dubai telehealth scope and emergency/controlled-medication exclusions.

exact_sections.heading: 6. Red Flags
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists respiratory, swallowing, neurologic, rash, and pediatric breathing concerns that require assessment or escalation.

source_documents.population: Adults and children with common cold; severity caveats for neonates, older people, and long-term conditions.
source_documents.setting: Telehealth services in DHA-licensed health facilities.

population: Adults requiring general-practice symptom, prevention or result review.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.
source_documents.setting: Primary and community care with person-centred multimorbidity review.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.4 — multimorbidity, daily activities, falls, medicines, and frailty context
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting long-term-condition burden, day-to-day activity difficulty, support from multiple services, frailty or falls context, number of regular medicines, gait and self-reported health assessment when actually completed.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.8 — treatment burden, day-to-day life, carers, goals, values, and priorities
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting functional impact, mental and physical health interaction, treatment burden, carer involvement, independence, social activity, personal goals, values, priorities, and medicine concerns.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.9–1.6.15 — medicines and treatment review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

source_documents.population: Adults with two or more long-term conditions, including frailty, falls, sensory impairment, chronic pain, mental health conditions, and treatment burden.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording the presenting complaint, investigations or procedures, outcome, follow-up, responsible party, referral and discharge destination in a discharge handover.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access type, access history, examination findings, flow or dysfunction observations and clinician interpretation without inferring access status.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — access planning and creation
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, access planning and creation recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting access planning, referral context, access maturation or intervention history and patient discussion.

exact_sections.heading: Vascular access guideline — complications and follow-up
exact_sections.locator: official guideline PDF, complication surveillance and follow-up recommendations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm or other access concerns and clinician-entered escalation or follow-up.

source_documents.population: Adults receiving or preparing for haemodialysis and their dialysis access care teams.
source_documents.setting: Nephrology, haemodialysis and vascular-access assessment and follow-up.

source_documents.source_organisation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
source_documents.source_document: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

exact_sections.heading: Detection of CKD and evaluation of chronicity
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

source_documents.population: Adults and children at risk of or living with CKD, with age, cause, GFR, albuminuria, progression, treatment, and referral qualifiers.
source_documents.setting: CKD detection, evaluation, monitoring, medication stewardship, referral, and longitudinal kidney care.

population: Adults requiring haemodialysis-session, access, adequacy or dialysis follow-up documentation.
exact_scope_qualifiers.transformation: Source prose is represented as optional clinician-entered documentation fields; no clinical inference is performed.

evidence_limitations: Does not create referrals or escalation automatically
